data.narrative:
Vivodyne, a Series A-stage biotech company founded by Andrei Georgescu and Dan Huh, has raised $78M+ to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 3 public peers in Biotech & Health (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L) and 8 private equivalents, though narrow-stage matching within the sector proved insufficient for reliable peer-median triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable valuation anchor. Using total capital raised ($78M) as a Series A baseline and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of progression to the next financing stage yields $156M. This method assumes comparable burn rates and dilution patterns across early-stage biotech.

Public-comp anchoring cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely publish. The median P/S multiple across the public Biotech & Health set is 8.1x; however, applying this metric requires Vivodyne's top-line data.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $133M to $179M, centered on $156M. This range reflects a ±15% sensitivity band around the stage-progression output. Key uncertainties include the actual cash burn rate relative to peer cohorts, revenue trajectory visibility, and the timing assumptions embedded in the 2.0x multiplier. A full peer-median method would strengthen conviction but requires either a larger adjacent-stage private comp set or target revenue disclosure.
